{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Licence Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings, redline positions and open items

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 findings. Ten rules are compliant as drafted (several because the Agreement is silent where silence favours us, and several because they sit at the fallback). Six clauses are deviations and two rules are unaddressed entirely.

The commercial risk concentrates in three critical items. First, risk allocation is materially one-sided: the only liability cap limits TrueLink alone and only for certain sections, leaving our liability — including a very broad Client indemnity — uncapped. Second, TrueLink gives no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, while Client indemnifies broadly. Third, on intellectual property, Section 8(d) grants TrueLink an independent right to distribute, license, resell and exploit Credit Data, and there is no ownership or assignment clause for the customisation work product we pay for. We also need to fix assignment (no successor carve-out for Client), licence scope (no affiliate or successor coverage), the absence of any performance warranty (only a Year 2000 warranty), and the complete absence of exit/data-return and insurance provisions.

We recommend pressing all three critical items plus transition assistance as gating; the balance are ordinary redlines with fallbacks available.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / our position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | TrueLink's indemnity is limited to its own breach or failure to perform, with no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere; Client's indemnity is broad. We add a TrueLink defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement (Interface, Hosting and Support Services), breach of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client data, and gross negligence/willful misconduct, with notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics, and narrow Client's indemnity to Client Content and Client's violation of law. We take the preferred position rather than the fallback because the fallback's 3x-fees super-cap would newly cap a presently uncapped indemnity. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | The only cap is one-sided (TrueLink only, and only for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11); Client's liability, including its § 12a indemnity, is uncapped, and there is no indirect/consequential damages exclusion anywhere. We target the fallback: retain the 12-month compensation basis verbatim, make the cap mutual and aggregate, and place indemnification, confidentiality (§ 10), gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap for both parties. Preferred upgrades (USD 1,000,000 floor, mutual consequential exclusion, data protection/fraud/IP carve-outs, payment-obligation exclusion) remain available. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Section 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to distribute, disseminate, license, resell and exploit Credit Data, beyond what is needed to deliver the services and not cured by § 10(c) confidentiality; there is no ownership or assignment clause for the customisation work product we pay for, no statement that Client retains data rights, and no bar on joint ownership. We add Client ownership of work product with assignment and a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded TrueLink IP, confirm Client's retained data rights and no joint ownership, and narrow the Credit Data licence to processing solely to provide the services. TrueLink's ownership of the Interface under § 2(d) is preserved. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Section 15 is the only assignment provision and has no successor carve-out, so a merger, acquisition or asset sale by Client needs TrueLink's approval, with no reasonableness standard. We take the preferred position: Client may assign without approval to an affiliate or M&A/asset-sale successor; TrueLink may assign only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor of ours; a change of control of Client gives TrueLink no termination right. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | The § 2(a) grant runs only to "Client" (Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.), with no affiliate or contractor coverage and no notice mechanism, and § 15 bars transfer of rights, including to an M&A successor. We propose the shortest fallback cure: a new § 2(e) extending the licence to Client affiliates on written notice and permitting a Client-only transfer to an M&A successor, without expanding TrueLink's assignment rights in § 15. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | The only Vendor warranty is the Year 2000 warranty in § 9; there is no documentation-conformance or services warranty and no repair/replace or refund remedy (§ 3 hosting commitments are "reasonable commercial efforts" only, and § 2(i)/3(h) disclaim data accuracy). We insert the fallback warranty (90-day software conformance, 30-day services, repair/replacement or refund). The disclaimer is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT", so no carve-out edit is needed. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No exit mechanic exists. Section 14 only continues services to month-end following notice, and § 13 puts the burden on Client to arrange a new name server (30 days) and hosting environment (60 days). There is no transition assistance, no data return or export in a usable format, and no certified deletion (§ 10 has no return-of-materials mechanic). We insert a short provision after the Termination section meeting the preferred elements. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | The Agreement contains no insurance obligation at all, yet TrueLink hosts our web site and transmits and stores borrower credit data. We insert a preferred-level clause (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Client data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), offering the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback in the comment. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Client; § 2(a) is non-exclusive and expressly preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services. § 3(i) bites only where we voluntarily use the Interface. Nothing to redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds Client; § 2(a) meets the preferred position. Diligence note: the separate "Non-Competition Agreement" referenced in § 8(d) is not included here and should be checked for any covenant binding Client. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No liquidated damages or penalties on Client. Section 14 termination carries no fee or make-whole; § 7/§ 8(f) anti-spam terms carry no monetary penalty; § 5(a) minimums are ongoing service fees. Note the blank $ minimums (§ 5(a)) and blank Support Services term (§ 4) for commercial completion. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Section 14 gives Client an unconditional termination election on notice (service ends the last day of the month following notice), with no early-termination fee; TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right. Meets the fallback on every material term. Drafting query: § 14's "Subject to Section 4" and § 2(c)'s cross-reference to "section 12" appear to be stale references. |
| Medium | RENEWAL | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Section 13: one-year initial term, successive 12-month renewals, 30-day non-renewal notice either side; no unilateral uplift right (fees fixed by Exhibit A/B, § 6 price freeze and best-customer rate, § 16 written-amendment requirement). Preferred-only gaps (no Vendor renewal reminder, no CPI/3% uplift cap) noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant (fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5(a) sets a monthly fee floor, so this sits at the fallback rather than preferred: single 12-month term (§ 13), short-notice Client exit (§ 14), and a true-up with no shortfall penalty or acceleration. We should confirm the blank minimum amounts and the § 4 Support Services period before signature. |
| Medium | GOVLAW | Compliant (fallback) | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law (§ 26) with exclusive jurisdiction in San Luis Obispo County (§ 27) is an accepted law and corresponding forum; no arbitration provision exists. Falls short of preferred (New York) and lacks an injunctive-relief venue carve-out — noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | The only MFN runs in our favour (§ 6 best-customer rate plus a one-year price freeze); no Customer MFN obligation. Benefit to us — no redline. |
| Medium | AUDIT | Compliant (better than preferred) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No Vendor audit, inspection or records-access right; information flows favour us (§ 6 charge documentation and contest right, § 3(e) usage statistics and raw logs). If the pricing exhibits later introduce self-reported volumes, confirm no audit right is added. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds Client; § 8 covenants and § 10 confidentiality impose no hiring restriction. Preferred position already met. |

## Walk-away items

Three findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **Liability allocation (LOL-CAP, § 12 INDEMNITY.)** — Client uncapped while TrueLink is capped. We require a mutual, aggregate cap on the existing 12-month basis, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct carved out for both parties.
2. **No data return on exit (TRANSITION, § 12 INDEMNITY.)** — no obligation to return or export our data or to certify deletion. We require the inserted transition assistance, data return and certified deletion provision.
3. **No Vendor insurance (INSURANCE, § 12 INDEMNITY.)** — no cover at all where TrueLink hosts our site and processes borrower credit data. We require the inserted insurance clause; the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback is available.

We would also treat the absence of any TrueLink IP infringement indemnity (INDEMN) and the Credit Data exploitation right plus missing work-product ownership (IP) as must-fix given the data and deliverables at stake.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the six deviations and two missing clauses (INDEMN, LOL-CAP, IP, ASSIGN, LICENSE, WARRANTY, TRANSITION, INSURANCE), with `[Playbook]` comments stating the position and the fallback where one is offered.
2. Flag the three walk-away items to the business owner before we send, so escalation authority is agreed in advance.
3. Close the commercial blanks with the business: the § 5(a) monthly minimum amounts and the § 4 Support Services period.
4. Obtain and review the separate "Non-Competition Agreement" referenced in § 8(d) for any covenant binding Client.
5. Raise the non-substantive drafting queries: stale cross-references in § 14 ("Subject to Section 4") and § 2(c) ("section 12").
6. Monitor: if pricing exhibits are completed with self-reported volumes, confirm no Vendor audit right is introduced; if one is proposed, hold it to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site, independent auditor, at TrueLink's cost absent a 5% underpayment."}
